title: External crate dependencies can be misclassified as internal project edges when names collide

evidence.quote: it("emits external edges for registry deps", async () => {
it("does not emit edges from a registry package that shares a workspace name", async () => {

reasoning: createDependencies checks projects[dep.name] before checking whether the dependency itself is external. In a workspace with project `util`, if another workspace package depends on a registry or git crate also named `util`, the dependency is emitted as `app -> util` instead of `app -> cargo:util`. That corrupts the Nx graph by adding a false internal workspace dependency and hiding the real external dependency edge. The included tests cover normal path dependencies, normal registry dependencies, and registry package entries that share a workspace package name, but not the direct dependency-name collision path that triggers this branch order bug.
reproduction: Mock cargo metadata with workspace packages `app` and `util`; make `app.dependencies` contain `{ name: "util", source: "registry+https://crates.io", kind: null }`; pass ctx.projects containing both `app` and `util` plus ctx.externalNodes containing `cargo:util`. createDependencies currently emits target `util` because the project-name lookup runs before external classification.
recommendation: In createDependencies, classify the dependency before the project-name lookup. Only emit an internal project edge when `!isExternal(dep, workspaceRoot)` and `projects[dep.name]` exists; for external dependencies, build `cargo:${dep.name}` and use ctx.externalNodes. Add the collision regression before changing the branch order.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The registry dependency test has only `app` in ctx.projects, so projects[dep.name] is false. The collision-adjacent test covers an external package entry that shares a workspace package name, not an external direct dependency whose name collides with a workspace project.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a createDependencies test where `app` depends on registry `util` while a workspace project named `util` also exists; assert the edge target is `cargo:util` and not `util`.
minimumFixScope: Update createDependencies dependency classification and add one focused graph.spec.ts regression.
